answers.answer: Excalidraw is an open-source, hand-drawn-style canvas whiteboard for diagrams and wireframes, with shapes, images, libraries, undo/redo and PNG/SVG/JSON export. The project supplies the excalidraw.com browser app, adding offline/PWA use, encrypted real-time collaboration, browser autosave and shareable links. Developers embed its React npm package. The pinned README lists Google Cloud, Meta, CodeSandbox, Obsidian Excalidraw, Replit, Slite, Notion and HackerRank as integrators; this is repository testimony, not live deployment verification.

Principal boundaries: excalidraw-app is the hosted application, wiring the editor to collaboration and local/backend storage; packages/excalidraw supplies the embeddable React editor, composing App with initialization/state providers and exporting restoration, serialization and UI APIs; packages/element contains element algorithms and exposes geometry, binding, resizing, rendering, Scene and store modules; common supplies shared functions/constants; math supplies 2D mathematical helpers; utils supplies utility/export functions. These are package/component responsibilities, not independently deployed backend services.

A Yarn 1.22.22 workspace monorepo separates excalidraw-app, packages/* and examples/*. Sources use TypeScript/TSX with React, JavaScript build scripts, and CSS/SCSS styling. TypeScript uses strict mode, react-jsx and bundler resolution, with aliases for common, excalidraw, element, fractional-indexing, laser-pointer, math and utils. Vite builds/serves the application; esbuild plus its Sass plugin emits the editor's ESM development/production bundles, and tsc generates declarations. Vitest, ESLint and Prettier provide tests/checks. The app pins React 19; the library declares React 17/18/19 peer compatibility. Build configuration is evidence of intended organization, not a build executed here.

Public-library callers import restoreElements from @excalidraw/excalidraw. Its source entry packages/excalidraw/index.tsx re-exports the named function from ./data/restore; there is no forwarding wrapper there. The implementation is packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts:891. The package's root exports resolve to dist/dev/index.js or dist/prod/index.js, while the repository's TypeScript alias resolves to index.tsx.

Implemented by isInvisiblySmallElement in packages/element/src/sizeHelpers.ts. For line, arrow or freedraw, fewer than two points qualifies; additionally, an arrow with exactly two points qualifies when each endpoint coordinate differs by strictly less than 0.1 (pointsEqual's coordinate-wise tolerance). Other elements qualify only when both width and height equal zero. Thus a zero-width but nonzero-height rectangle does not qualify, and neither do two-point lines/freedraw merely because their endpoints coincide. This is geometric classification, not an opacity, zoom, viewport or rendered-pixel test.

@excalidraw/element directly declares @excalidraw/common 0.18.0, @excalidraw/math 0.18.0 and @excalidraw/fractional-indexing 3.3.0. The owning manifest names @excalidraw/element and lists these under dependencies: element → those packages, not the reverse. A type-only import of editor types in sizeHelpers does not establish an additional declared manifest dependency.

Public barrel → restoreElements → restoreElement's rectangle branch → restoreElementWithProperties normalizes a clone. Back in restoreElements, X checks the ORIGINAL rectangle. For width=height=0 and the flag true, it bumps the migrated record's version, sets isDeleted=true, and pushes it into the result—not an empty array. Index synchronization follows; without repairBindings it returns immediately. Selection is skipped; unsupported/failed migrations are omitted. Boundaries: public API → restoration → element package. bumpVersion uses the supplied local version or restored version, adds one, refreshes nonce/timestamp; index repair can increment again. This is a static path, not proof of UI removal, persistence or collaboration delivery.

restore.ts imports Y through @excalidraw/element and calls it in restoreElements' deletion guard. packages/element/src/index.ts imports Y directly and getVisibleElements uses it to exclude small elements alongside deleted ones; the same barrel re-exports sizeHelpers. getNonDeletedElements only checks deletion. A changed Y can therefore change those two direct decisions when reached. Wider rendering/export/storage/collaboration effects remain inferred unless their callers and runtime inputs are traced; this is not an exhaustive repository-wide consumer list.

packages/excalidraw/tests/data/restore.test.ts has the test named 'should return empty array when isInvisiblySmallElement is true'. It creates a rectangle, forces the spied predicate to return true, and calls restoreElements with deleteInvisibleElements=true. Despite its stale name, the assertion expects one record containing isDeleted:true. The spy is reset before each test and restored afterward. This exercises restoration's reaction to the predicate result, not real zero dimensions, point-count/tolerance classification, rendering, or an end-to-end import. No test was executed in this trial.

Z enters restoreElements as its optional third-argument property and is forwarded to restoreElement. After migration it gates Y, then version bump and isDeleted=true; the element remains returned. Missing/false Z bypasses that guard. The text branch separately deletes empty text under Z. A concrete caller is app initializeScene, setting Z=true for local-storage and backend restoration.
